subject_offered_enrollment_rank.name: subject_offered_enrollment_rank
subject_offered_enrollment_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,
  subject_offered.TERM_CODE,
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID,
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY subject_offered.TERM_CODE ORDER BY COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,0) DESC) AS enrollment_rank
FROM subject_offered

params.description: Ranks subjects within each term by number of enrolled students, returning one row per subject_offered summary with its term, id, title, enrolled count, and enrollment rank.
params.when_to_use: Find the most- or least-enrolled subjects in a specific term (top-N / bottom-N by enrollment). | Annotate subject_offered rows with their position (rank) in enrollment within the same term for reporting or filtering (e.g., top 10 subjects this term). | Compose into higher-level queries that need a stable per-subject-offering enrollment rank (e.g., join to subject metadata or faculty and then filter where enrollment_rank <= N).
params.output_schema: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY: surrogate key identifying the subject_offered summary row; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY. | subject_offered.TERM_CODE: academic term code for the offered subject; sourced directly from subject_offered.TERM_CODE. Used as the RANK() partition key. | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID: subject identifier (e.g., course/subject code) for the offered subject; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID. | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE: descriptive title of the subject offering; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE. | subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS: count of enrolled students for this subject_offered summary; sourced directly from subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS and used to compute the rank (NULL treated as 0 via COALESCE in ordering). | enrollment_rank: integer rank within term (1 = highest enrollment) computed as RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY term_code ORDER BY COALESCE(num_enrolled_students,0) DESC). Ties receive the same rank and leave gaps according to RANK semantics.
params.metric: enrollment_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY subject_offered.TERM_CODE ORDER BY COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0) DESC) | NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS = base column subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS (used as the ordering metric; NULLs treated as 0 for ranking)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to subject_offered_core on subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY = subject_offered_core.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY — safe because this view is one-row-per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, so joining to a one-row-per-same-key source preserves cardinality and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to subject_summary_core on subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID = subject_summary_core.SUBJECT_ID (and optionally TERM_CODE = subject_summary_core.TERM_CODE if that view is term-scoped) — safe if subject_summary_core is one-row-per subject_id (or per subject_id+term) so the subject_offered measures are not multiplied. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many children (e.g., a raw enrollments table, sections, or faculty assignments) without re-aggregation because those joins can duplicate NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS and invalidate enrollment_rank. If you must bring one-to-many detail in, either: |   - aggregate the child to one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY first (e.g., SUM or COUNT) and then join, or |   - join and then re-aggregate the joined result back to subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, recalculating measures/metrics you need. | If composing further ranking or window functions partitioned by TERM_CODE, use this view's enrollment_rank as a stable input but be mindful that re-partitioning or re-aggregation may change rank semantics (e.g., RANK() vs DENSE_RANK()). | When joining to subject_offered_with_faculty (a JOIN sibling), ensure the join keys produce at most one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY on the right side; if subject_offered_with_faculty contains multiple faculty rows per subject_offered summary, aggregate faculty (e.g., STRING_AGG or choose a primary faculty) before joining to avoid duplicating enrollment counts and altering ranks.

subject_offered_enrollment_rank.description: Per TERM_CODE ranking of subject_offered by NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS with an explicit rank column. Use this to pick top-k subjects per term by filtering on rank. | Use for: Find top-enrolled subjects per term; Investigate enrollment distribution across terms; Select top-k rows per TERM_CODE for downstream joins

  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN,
  subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM subject_summary

params.description: One-row-per-subject-summary: aggregated subject-level enrollments, units, and identifiers for a term (subject_summary rows).
params.when_to_use: Report subject-level enrollment and unit totals for a given term (e.g., total students in a subject, first-week vs fifth-week enrollment). | Build dashboards that list subjects with their units and enrollment metrics (sorting, filtering by term, master subject grouping). | Compose higher-level aggregates (e.g., college or department totals) by further aggregating this view's enrollment/units. | Join subject-level attributes (title, ids, sort keys) to other datasets while preserving aggregated enrollment measures if join is 1:1.
params.output_schema: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY: surrogate primary key for the subject_summary row (grain). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_summary.TERM_CODE: academic term identifier for the summary row. Source column: subject_summary.TERM_CODE | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID: subject code (e.g., MATH). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT: sort key for subject id ordering. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE: human-readable subject title. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID: master/normalized subject identifier used for grouping variants. Source column: subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT: sort key for master subject ordering. Source column: subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS: total units associated with the subject summary (aggregated units measure). Source column: subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS | subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS: units attributable to lecture component. Source column: subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS | subject_summary.LAB_UNITS: units attributable to lab component. Source column: subject_summary.LAB_UNITS | subject_summary.PREP_UNITS: units attributable to preparation component. Source column: subject_summary.PREP_UNITS | subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS: units attributable to design component. Source column: subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER: numeric count of enrolled students in the subject (aggregate at this row's grain). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER: enrollment count for the subject cluster (if clustering applied). Source column: subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK: enrollment count measured in first week. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK: enrollment count measured in fifth week. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT: count of credit enrollments. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN: count of 'listen' (audit/non-credit) enrollments. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN | subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE: ETL load date for the row. Source column: subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.grounded_columns: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_summary.TERM_CODE | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS | subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS | subject_summary.LAB_UNITS | subject_summary.PREP_UNITS | subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN | subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.metric: TOTAL_UNITS = subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS  -- stored aggregate (units) at the subject_summary grain | LECTURE_UNITS = subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS  -- stored units for lecture portion | LAB_UNITS = subject_summary.LAB_UNITS  -- stored units for lab portion | PREP_UNITS = subject_summary.PREP_UNITS  -- stored units for prep portion | DESIGN_UNITS = subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS  -- stored units for design portion | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER  -- stored aggregate count of enrolled students | CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER = subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER  -- stored cluster-level enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK  -- stored first-week enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK  -- stored fifth-week enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT  -- stored credit enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN  -- stored listen/audit enrollment count
params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins (do NOT duplicate measures): |  - Join to dimension-like, one-row-per-key tables/views on matching keys (example): join to a term dimension on TERM_CODE, or to a subject dimension on SUBJECT_ID or MASTER_SUBJECT_ID — safe because subject_summary is one-row-per SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY (one-row-per subject_summary) so joining 1:1 preserves measures. |  - Join to subject_offered_core on SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY (if subject_offered_core is one-row-per-SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) — safe only if that sibling view is known to be 1:1 with subject_summary; verify sibling grain before joining. |  | Do NOT join (without re-aggregation) to known one-to-many tables/views because they will multiply this view's measures: |  - Do NOT directly join to subject_offered_with_faculty (JOIN) if that view contains one row per offering or per faculty assignment (one-to-many to subject_summary) unless you first aggregate the many-side back to subject_summary grain. Joining without re-aggregation will over-count SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_* and UNIT measures. |  - Do NOT join to subject_offered_enrollment_rank (RANK) if it is one-row-per-offering/rank (one-to-many) without reducing it to the subject_summary grain first. If you need per-offering details, compute offering-level metrics separately and avoid summing subject_summary metrics with those rows. |  | Guidance for safe composition by planners: |  - If you need to combine subject_summary metrics with a one-to-many sibling, perform an aggregated subquery on the many-side grouped to SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY before joining, e.g.: SELECT s.*, m.some_agg FROM subject_summary s LEFT JOIN (SELECT SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY, SUM(x) AS some_agg FROM many_table GROUP BY SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) m USING (SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY). This preserves the one-row-per-subject_summary property. |  - When computing higher-level aggregates (e.g., totals by MASTER_SUBJECT_ID or TERM_CODE), aggregate the subject_summary measures (SUM(TOTAL_UNITS), SUM(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER), etc.) grouped by the desired key — do not rely on joins to expand rows and then SUM without DISTINCT control. |  - Treat SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY as the canonical grain key for row-level uniqueness. Any join that is many-to-one into subject_summary (many rows on the other side per SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) must be pre-aggregated back to SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY to avoid duplication.

params.description: Provides one-row-per-subject_offered summary including the responsible faculty identifiers and their directory details (if available).
params.when_to_use: Look up the responsible faculty contact info for a specific subject offering (by SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, TERM_CODE, or SUBJECT_ID). | Build reports that display subject offerings alongside faculty name, email, office and phone when each subject_offered row should stay at the subject_offered grain. | Compose further SQL that filters or aggregates subject_offered-level measures while also showing faculty attributes (safe when not introducing one-to-many expansions).
params.output_schema: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY: unique key for this subject_offered row — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_offered.TERM_CODE: term code for the subject offering — derived directly from subject_offered.TERM_CODE | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID: subject identifier (e.g., subject code) — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE: title of the subject offered — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID: MIT ID of the responsible faculty for the subject offering — derived directly from subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME: responsible faculty name as stored on the subject_offered row — derived directly from subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME | employee_directory.MIT_ID: MIT ID from employee_directory (may be NULL if no matching directory row) — derived directly from employee_directory.MIT_ID | employee_directory.LAST_NAME: last name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.LAST_NAME | employee_directory.FIRST_NAME: first name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.FULL_NAME: full name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.FULL_NAME | employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION: office location from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION | employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE: office phone from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS: email address from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS
params.grounded_columns: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_offered.TERM_CODE | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME | employee_directory.MIT_ID | employee_directory.LAST_NAME | employee_directory.FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.FULL_NAME | employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION | employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS
params.metric: This view does not define any aggregated metrics. All outputs are directly selected base columns (no aggregates). If you need counts or sums, compute them by aggregating subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY (one row per key) after applying any additional joins/filters.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional lookups that are one-to-one with subject_offered keys — safe because this view is one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY so measures at that grain are not duplicated. | Safe to join on subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY to: subject_offered_core (SEL) — safe because subject_offered_core is a same-grain selection/view over subject_offered (one row per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY). | Safe to join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY to other one-row-per-subject_offered views (for example, subject_summary_core) provided they are defined at the same SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY grain. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables or views (for example: enrollments, meeting times, student lists, or any view that aggregates at a lower-grain such as per-student or per-meeting) without re-aggregation because such joins will multiply subject_offered rows and thereby duplicate any derived counts or measures. If you need to combine with a one-to-many relationship, first aggregate the many-side to one row per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY (for example: COUNT(*) AS enrollment_count FROM enrollment GROUP BY SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY) and then join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY. | If joining to employee_directory variants: this view already left-joins employee_directory by MIT_ID = subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID. Re-joining to employee_directory on the same MIT_ID is redundant. If you need additional employee attributes that exist in another employee view keyed by MIT_ID and guaranteed one-row-per-MIT_ID, you can inner-join on RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = other_employee.MIT_ID safely (one-to-one). | If you must join to subject_offered_enrollment_rank (RANK) which is likely one-row-per-subject_offered (ranked metric): verify it is one-row-per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY before joining directly; if it is per-subject_offered then join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY is safe. If it is one-to-many, aggregate first.

subject_materials_denorm.body_sql:
SELECT

  cso.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  tm.`TITLE` AS TITLE,

  tm.`USED_SHELF_PRICE` AS USED_SHELF_PRICE,
  tm.`RENTAL_NEW_PRICE` AS RENTAL_NEW_PRICE,
  tm.`RENTAL_USED_PRICE` AS RENTAL_USED_PRICE
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered` cso
-- bring in canonical subject title from cis_course_catalog (required output column source)
LEFT JOIN `cis_course_catalog` ccc
  ON cso.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = ccc.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
    AND cso.`TERM_CODE` = ccc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`
-- join section-level library reserve/material link table to reach materials; allows one row per SECTION_ID
LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_matrl_detail` lrm
  ON cso.`SECTION_ID` = lrm.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
    AND cso.`TERM_CODE` = lrm.`TERM_CODE`
    AND cso.`SUBJECT_ID` = lrm.`SUBJECT_ID`
-- join library subject offered to relate to specific course-offering material rows (if present)
LEFT JOIN `library_subject_offered` lso
  ON lrm.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = lso.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
    AND lso.`TERM_CODE` = cso.`TERM_CODE`
-- join reserve catalog to get ISBN/title equivalents when materials are reserve-catalog based
LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_catalog` lrc
  ON lrm.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = lrc.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
-- join TIP detail/material for explicit material records and pricing (primary source for material title/isbn/prices)

  ON cso.`TERM_CODE` = td.`TERM_CODE`
    AND cso.`SUBJECT_ID` = td.`SUBJECT_ID`
    AND cso.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = td.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
-- join tip_material to get price and title fields when available
LEFT JOIN `tip_material` tm
  ON td.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` = tm.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`

buildings_canonical.name: buildings_canonical
buildings_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  `FAC_BUILDING_KEY`,
  `BUILDING_NAME_LONG`,
  -- canonicalize DATE_BUILT to ISO YYYY-MM-DD where possible; keep original string if unparsable
  CASE
    WHEN `DATE_BUILT` REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$' THEN `DATE_BUILT`
    WHEN `DATE_BUILT` REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}/[0-9]{2}/[0-9]{2}$' THEN REPLACE(`DATE_BUILT`, '/', '-')
    WHEN `DATE_BUILT` REGEXP '^[0-9]{2}/[0-9]{2}/[0-9]{4}$' THEN DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(`DATE_BUILT`, '%m/%d/%Y'), '%Y-%m-%d')
    WHEN `DATE_BUILT` REGEXP '^[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}$' THEN DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(`DATE_BUILT`, '%m-%d-%Y'), '%Y-%m-%d')
    WHEN `DATE_BUILT` REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}$' THEN CONCAT(`DATE_BUILT`, '-01-01')
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `DATE_BUILT`,
  -- NUM_OF_ROOMS numeric canonicalization: keep integer when present, NULL when not numeric
  CASE
    WHEN `NUM_OF_ROOMS` IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE `NUM_OF_ROOMS`
  END AS `NUM_OF_ROOMS`
FROM `fac_building`

iap_category_year_aggs.name: iap_category_year_aggs
iap_category_year_aggs.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC AS MAJOR_USE_DESC,
  fr.FLOOR AS FLOOR,
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS FAC_ROOM_KEY,
  -- grouping keys
  COALESCE(iapcat.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME, '') AS IAP_CATEGORY_NAME,
  -- academic year literal(s) should be provided when querying the view; expose TERM_CODE so callers can derive year externally
  so.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  -- aggregations per (category, academic year)
  SUM(COALESCE(iapdet.FEE,0)) AS SUM_FEE,
  COUNT(DISTINCT so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY) AS DISTINCT_SUBJECT_OFFERED_COUNT,
  MIN(so.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER) AS MIN_SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,
  MAX(so.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER) AS MAX_SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER
FROM iap_subject_detail iapdet
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_category iapcat
  ON iapdet.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = iapcat.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
LEFT JOIN subject_offered so
  ON iapdet.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
  AND iapdet.ACTIVITY_TITLE = so.SUBJECT_TITLE
  -- note: caller must ensure proper join keys for subject offered; we preserve original columns
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr
  ON so.MEET_PLACE = fr.ROOM
GROUP BY
  fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC,
  fr.FLOOR,
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY,
  COALESCE(iapcat.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME, ''),
  so.TERM_CODE
iap_category_year_aggs.description: Aggregated measures per IAP category name and academic year: raw sum of fee amounts, count of distinct canonical subject identifiers, min and max enrollment across offerings. SELECT

  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,

  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE` AS `LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
WHERE
  -- Only include rows that indicate they are offered in IAP (non-null/true-ish flag)
  (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP`) <> '')
  -- Exclude rows with null/empty or clearly non-physical MEET_PLACE values
  AND (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE`) <> ''
    AND UPPER(TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE`)) NOT IN ('TBA','TBD','ONLINE','VIRTUAL','REMOTE','--'))
  -- Ensure there's a section-level grain value
  AND (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID`) <> '')

meet_place_building_link.name: meet_place_building_link
meet_place_building_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  c.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered c
LEFT JOIN buildings b
  ON (
    -- match when MEET_PLACE contains the building number as a whole token (space, start, end, or punctuation)
    c.MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL
    AND b.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
    AND (
      c.MEET_PLACE = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
      OR c.MEET_PLACE LIKE CONCAT(b.BUILDING_NUMBER, ' %')
      OR c.MEET_PLACE LIKE CONCAT('% ', b.BUILDING_NUMBER)
      OR c.MEET_PLACE LIKE CONCAT('% ', b.BUILDING_NUMBER, ' %')
      OR c.MEET_PLACE LIKE CONCAT('%(', b.BUILDING_NUMBER, ')%')
      OR c.MEET_PLACE LIKE CONCAT('%-', b.BUILDING_NUMBER, '-%')
      OR c.MEET_PLACE LIKE CONCAT('%/', b.BUILDING_NUMBER, '/%')
      OR c.MEET_PLACE LIKE CONCAT('%#', b.BUILDING_NUMBER, '#%')
      -- also try matching building number at start or end with punctuation
      OR c.MEET_PLACE REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^0-9A-Za-z])', REPLACE(b.BUILDING_NUMBER, "'", "\\'"), '($|[^0-9A-Za-z])')
    )
  )
GROUP BY c.SECTION_ID, c.MEET_PLACE, b.BUILDING_NUMBER, b.BUILDING_NAME
meet_place_building_link.description: Denormalized mapping from a section/meeting (SECTION_ID) and its MEET_PLACE to a building (BUILDING_NAME and BUILDING_NUMBER) when MEET_PLACE appears to reference a building/room identifier. This view attempts to join MEET_PLACE values to BUILDING_NUMBER/BUILDING_NAME from buildings when MEET_PLACE contains that building number; it leaves building fields NULL when no match is found. One row per SECTION_ID.

iap_session_rows_selector.name: iap_session_rows_selector
iap_session_rows_selector.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccs.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  ccs.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  ccs.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  ccs.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  ccs.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  ccs.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  ccs.MEET_TIME AS MEET_TIME
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered AS ccs
WHERE
  -- restrict to IAP terms: lift literal out of view (caller should bind desired IAP term codes)
  /* Caller should replace the placeholder list with the actual IAP TERM_CODE(s), e.g. ('202201') */
  ccs.TERM_CODE IN ('__IAP_TERM_CODE_PLACEHOLDER__')
  -- consider virtual if MEET_PLACE or MEET_TIME mention online/virtual or explicit flags if present
  AND (
    -- explicit meet place indicating online
    ccs.MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL
    AND (
      LOWER(ccs.MEET_PLACE) LIKE '%online%'
      OR LOWER(ccs.MEET_PLACE) LIKE '%zoom%'
      OR LOWER(ccs.MEET_PLACE) LIKE '%virtual%'
      OR LOWER(ccs.MEET_PLACE) LIKE '%webex%'
      OR LOWER(ccs.MEET_PLACE) LIKE '%remote%'
      OR LOWER(ccs.MEET_PLACE) LIKE '%miteroom%'
      OR LOWER(ccs.MEET_PLACE) LIKE '%canvas%'
    )
    OR
    -- meet time containing online indicators
    (ccs.MEET_TIME IS NOT NULL AND (
      LOWER(ccs.MEET_TIME) LIKE '%online%'
      OR LOWER(ccs.MEET_TIME) LIKE '%virtual%'
      OR LOWER(ccs.MEET_TIME) LIKE '%zoom%'
      OR LOWER(ccs.MEET_TIME) LIKE '%webex%'
      OR LOWER(ccs.MEET_TIME) LIKE '%remote%'
    ))
  )

semantic_filters.term_contains: IAP (term identifier or TERM_CODE contains 'IAP' or equals 'IAP')
semantic_filters.virtual_indicators: rows where IS_LECTURE_SECTION/IS_LAB_SECTION etc. may be present but selection uses MEET_PLACE LIKE '%Virtual%' OR MEET_PLACE LIKE '%Online%' OR MEET_TIME LIKE '%Online%'

iap_subjects_session_cohort.name: iap_subjects_session_cohort
iap_subjects_session_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  cco.SUBJECT_ID           AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cco.SUBJECT_CODE         AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  cco.SECTION_ID           AS SECTION_ID,
  COUNT(DISTINCT iss.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY) AS SESSION_COUNT,
  COALESCE(SUM(isd.FEE),0)                       AS TOTAL_FEES,
  MIN(
    CASE
      WHEN iss.SESSION_START_TIME <> '' AND iss.SESSION_END_TIME <> '' THEN
        -- attempt to parse times as HH:MM[:SS], fallback NULL
        TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE,
          STR_TO_DATE(iss.SESSION_START_TIME, '%H:%i:%s'),
          STR_TO_DATE(iss.SESSION_END_TIME, '%H:%i:%s')
        )
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ) AS MIN_SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES,
  MAX(
    CASE
      WHEN iss.SESSION_START_TIME <> '' AND iss.SESSION_END_TIME <> '' THEN
        TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE,
          STR_TO_DATE(iss.SESSION_START_TIME, '%H:%i:%s'),
          STR_TO_DATE(iss.SESSION_END_TIME, '%H:%i:%s')
        )
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ) AS MAX_SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cco
JOIN iap_subject_detail isd
  ON isd.TERM_CODE = cco.TERM_CODE
  AND isd.ACTIVITY_TITLE = cco.SUBJECT_ID
  -- NOTE: iap_subject_detail does not store SUBJECT_ID column; matching is by provided fields above.
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_session iss
  ON iss.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = isd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
WHERE
  -- Lifted literals should be provided at query time; here we filter to subjects that have any linked session
  -- Keep no hard-coded term or other literals so the view is general-purpose
  (isd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NOT NULL OR iss.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NOT NULL)
GROUP BY
  cco.SUBJECT_ID,
  cco.SUBJECT_CODE,
  cco.SECTION_ID

semantic_filters.cohort_basis: rows limited to IAP virtual sessions (expected to be applied by joining or filtering the selector view or by the same TERM_CODE and MEET_PLACE filters)

iap_subjects_session_cohort.description: One row per subject participating in virtual IAP sessions. Aggregates session-level measures (count of sessions per subject, sum of fees per subject, min/max session duration per subject) but leaves final cross-subject totals to question-level ops.

SELECT

  fo.`ORGANIZATION_ID` AS ORGANIZATION_ID,
  -- fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_NAME -> alias as ORGANIZATION_NAME
  fo.`ORGANIZATION_NAME` AS ORGANIZATION_NAME,
  -- fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_NAME (second required) -> alias again as ORGANIZATION_NAME_DUP
  fo.`ORGANIZATION_NAME` AS ORGANIZATION_NAME_DUP,
  -- fclt_major_use.MAJOR_USE -> alias as MAJOR_USE
  mu.`MAJOR_USE` AS MAJOR_USE,
  -- fclt_major_use.MAJOR_USE (second required) -> alias again as MAJOR_USE_DUP
  mu.`MAJOR_USE` AS MAJOR_USE_DUP
FROM
  `fclt_organization` AS fo
  LEFT JOIN `fclt_major_use` AS mu
    ON (NULLIF(mu.`MAJOR_USE`, '') = NULLIF(fo.`MAJOR_ORG`, ''))
WHERE
  -- normalize empty string keys to NULL for grouping keys semantics:
  (fo.`FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY` IS NOT NULL)

If a real course table exists elsewhere, the final query should use that table. subject_school_link_candidates.name: subject_school_link_candidates
subject_school_link_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccc.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  ccc.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  ccc.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  ccc.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  ccc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  dcc.SCHOOL_WIDE_ELECTIVES AS SCHOOL_WIDE_ELECTIVES,
  -- carry through a SECTION_ID column to match requested grain (may be NULL when sourced from catalog)
  so.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID
FROM cis_course_catalog AS ccc
-- join to course_catalog_subject_offered to get TERM_CODE (match on subject identifiers)
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered AS cso
  ON cso.SUBJECT_ID = ccc.SUBJECT_ID
  AND cso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID <=> ccc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
  AND cso.DEPARTMENT_CODE <=> ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE
-- join to drupal_course_catalog to bring SCHOOL_WIDE_ELECTIVES (match on subject and subject number where possible)
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog AS dcc
  ON dcc.SUBJECT_ID = ccc.SUBJECT_ID
  AND dcc.SUBJECT_NUMBER <=> ccc.SUBJECT_NUMBER
-- left join subject_offered to carry SECTION_ID where there is a matching offered record
LEFT JOIN subject_offered AS so
  ON so.SUBJECT_ID = ccc.SUBJECT_ID
  AND so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID <=> ccc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
  AND so.COURSE_NUMBER <=> ccc.SUBJECT_NUMBER

LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog AS s
  ON s.SUBJECT_ID = c.SUBJECT_ID

Exposes subject identifiers, department code/name, offering-term flags and basic subject attributes so callers can classify 'TIP subjects' by availability.

course_section_current_term_cohort.name: course_section_current_term_cohort
course_section_current_term_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  c.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  c.HGN_CODE AS HGN_CODE,
  c.TOTAL_UNITS AS TOTAL_UNITS,

  c.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,

FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS c
WHERE
  /* restrict to rows marked as current term / this year:
     lift literals out of view, but rely on the stored flag columns here.
     Keep rows where the catalog indicates it is offered this year OR marked as offered for a regular/current term.
     Adjust caller-supplied predicate if a different definition is desired. */
  (c.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR = 'Y' OR c.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' OR c.IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM = 'Y' OR c.IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM = 'Y' OR c.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y')
  AND c.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL

iip_sessions_cohort.name: iip_sessions_cohort
iip_sessions_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  cco.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  cco.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  cco.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cco.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  cco.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  cco.IS_OFFERED_IAP AS IS_OFFERED_IAP,
  cco.TERM_DURATION AS TERM_DURATION,
  cco.MEET_TIME AS MEET_TIME,
  cco.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  dcc.SECTION_ID AS drupal_SECTION_ID,
  dcc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS drupal_MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  dcc.SUBJECT_ID AS drupal_SUBJECT_ID,
  dcc.SUBJECT_CODE AS drupal_SUBJECT_CODE,
  dcc.SUBJECT_TITLE AS drupal_SUBJECT_TITLE,
  dcc.IS_OFFERED_IAP AS drupal_IS_OFFERED_IAP,
  dcc.TERM_DURATION AS drupal_TERM_DURATION,
  dcc.MEET_TIME AS drupal_MEET_TIME,
  dcc.MEET_PLACE AS drupal_MEET_PLACE
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cco
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog dcc
  ON dcc.SECTION_ID = cco.SECTION_ID
    AND dcc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID <=> cco.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    AND dcc.SUBJECT_ID <=> cco.SUBJECT_ID
WHERE
  -- canonicalize common indicators of IAP offering without hardcoding institution-specific codes.
  (
    (cco.IS_OFFERED_IAP IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(UPPER(cco.IS_OFFERED_IAP)) IN ('Y','YES','TRUE','1','IAP'))
    OR
    (cco.TERM_DURATION IS NOT NULL AND INSTR(UPPER(cco.TERM_DURATION), 'IAP') > 0)
    OR
    (cco.MEET_TIME IS NOT NULL AND INSTR(UPPER(cco.MEET_TIME), 'IAP') > 0)
    OR
    (cco.MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL AND INSTR(UPPER(cco.MEET_PLACE), 'IAP') > 0)
  )
  OR
  (
    (dcc.IS_OFFERED_IAP IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(UPPER(dcc.IS_OFFERED_IAP)) IN ('Y','YES','TRUE','1','IAP'))
    OR
    (dcc.TERM_DURATION IS NOT NULL AND INSTR(UPPER(dcc.TERM_DURATION), 'IAP') > 0)
    OR
    (dcc.MEET_TIME IS NOT NULL AND INSTR(UPPER(dcc.MEET_TIME), 'IAP') > 0)
    OR
    (dcc.MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL AND INSTR(UPPER(dcc.MEET_PLACE), 'IAP') > 0)
  )
iip_sessions_cohort.description: One-row-per-session for sessions that are offered during IAP (Independent Activities Period). Filters canonicalize common IAP indicators but do not hard-code a single literal beyond matching 'IAP' or typical boolean markers for IAP offering.

SELECT

subject_iap_session_counts.name: subject_iap_session_counts

SELECT

  cco.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  cco.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  COUNT(iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY) AS total_sessions_for_subject
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered AS cco
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail AS iapd
  ON iapd.TERM_CODE = cco.TERM_CODE
     AND iapd.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE = iapd.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE -- noop to keep join logic explicit (no literal)
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_session AS iap
  ON iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = iapd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
     AND iap.SESSION_DATE IS NOT NULL
     AND iap.SESSION_DATE <> ''
WHERE cco.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  cco.SUBJECT_ID,
  cco.SUBJECT_CODE,
  cco.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  cco.SUBJECT_TITLE
subject_iap_session_counts.description: Aggregate counts of sessions per subject restricted to sessions that are IAP. One row per subject with a raw session count (no additional filtering or ordering). Used to supply total_sessions_for_subject for final answers.

tip_materials_rowlevel.name: tip_materials_rowlevel
tip_materials_rowlevel.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,

  c.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,

  AND c.`SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND c.`SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL

subject_material_status_agg.name: subject_material_status_agg
subject_material_status_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  ms.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  c.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  c.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  c.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  COUNT(DISTINCT m.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`) AS MATERIAL_COUNT,
  COUNT(DISTINCT so.`OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME`) AS DISTINCT_SCHOOL_COUNT,
  SUM(m.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE`) AS SUM_NEW_SHELF_PRICE,
  SUM(m.`USED_SHELF_PRICE`) AS SUM_USED_SHELF_PRICE,
  MIN(m.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE`) AS MIN_NEW_SHELF_PRICE,
  MIN(m.`USED_SHELF_PRICE`) AS MIN_USED_SHELF_PRICE,
  MAX(m.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE`) AS MAX_NEW_SHELF_PRICE,
  MAX(m.`USED_SHELF_PRICE`) AS MAX_USED_SHELF_PRICE,
  AVG(m.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE`) AS AVG_NEW_SHELF_PRICE,
  AVG(m.`USED_SHELF_PRICE`) AS AVG_USED_SHELF_PRICE,
  VARIANCE(m.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE`) AS VAR_NEW_SHELF_PRICE,
  VARIANCE(m.`USED_SHELF_PRICE`) AS VAR_USED_SHELF_PRICE,
  STDDEV(m.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE`) AS STDDEV_NEW_SHELF_PRICE,
  STDDEV(m.`USED_SHELF_PRICE`) AS STDDEV_USED_SHELF_PRICE
FROM tip_detail td
JOIN tip_material m
  ON td.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` = m.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`
JOIN tip_material_status ms
  ON td.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = ms.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
JOIN cis_course_catalog c
  ON td.`SUBJECT_ID` = c.`SUBJECT_ID`
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered so
  ON td.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = so.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
GROUP BY
  c.`SUBJECT_ID`,
  ms.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS`
subject_material_status_agg.description: Aggregated measures per subject and material status: sums, mins, maxes for numeric new/used shelf prices, counts of materials and distinct storefronts (schools). Intended to be computed from the TIP materials table joined to subject identifiers.

library_reserve_catalog_basic.body_sql:
SELECT

  -- preserve the stored catalog year column; parse to integer where possible, else NULL
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(CATALOG_YEAR) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN CATALOG_YEAR REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*-?[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$' THEN CAST(TRIM(CATALOG_YEAR) AS SIGNED)

  END AS CATALOG_YEAR,
  `CATALOG_TITLE` AS CATALOG_TITLE,
  `CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME` AS CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME
FROM `library_reserve_catalog`

buildings_street_addresses.name: buildings_street_addresses
buildings_street_addresses.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- assemble ADDRESS_LINE from fac_building_address stored street components as they appear in that table
  CONCAT(
    NULLIF(fba.STREET_NUMBER, ''),
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NUMBER <> '' AND fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX <> '' THEN CONCAT(fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN (fba.STREET_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NUMBER <> '') AND (fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL <> '') THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL) WHEN (fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL <> '') THEN fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN (fba.STREET_NAME IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NAME <> '') AND ( (fba.STREET_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NUMBER <> '') OR (fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL <> '') ) THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.STREET_NAME) WHEN (fba.STREET_NAME IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NAME <> '') THEN fba.STREET_NAME ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_SUFFIX <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.STREET_SUFFIX) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL) ELSE '' END
  ) AS ADDRESS_LINE,
  fba.CITY AS CITY,
  fba.STATE AS STATE,
  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  fba.BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY AS ADDRESS_ID
FROM buildings b
JOIN fac_building_address fba
  ON fba.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
WHERE fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET'

SELECT

  c.SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION AS SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION,
  c.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  c.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  c.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  c.IS_LECTURE_SECTION AS IS_LECTURE_SECTION,
  c.IS_LAB_SECTION AS IS_LAB_SECTION,
  c.IS_RECITATION_SECTION AS IS_RECITATION_SECTION,
  c.IS_DESIGN_SECTION AS IS_DESIGN_SECTION,
  c.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  c.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  c.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered c
WHERE
  (
    -- offered in a summer term by explicit summer flag (literal to be supplied at query time)
    c.IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM = 'Y'
    -- OR term code indicates a summer term pattern (literal matching strategy left to query-time)
    OR c.TERM_CODE LIKE 'SUM%'
    OR c.TERM_CODE LIKE 'S%'
    -- OR master subject / section records that are marked as offered this year but flagged for summer (kept generic)
    OR c.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR = 'Y'
  )

department_section_course_type_flags.name: department_section_course_type_flags

  MAX(CASE WHEN c.`IS_LECTURE_SECTION` IS NOT NULL AND c.`IS_LECTURE_SECTION` <> '' THEN c.`IS_LECTURE_SECTION` ELSE NULL END) AS `IS_LECTURE_SECTION`,
  MAX(CASE WHEN c.`IS_LAB_SECTION` IS NOT NULL AND c.`IS_LAB_SECTION` <> '' THEN c.`IS_LAB_SECTION` ELSE NULL END) AS `IS_LAB_SECTION`,
  MAX(CASE WHEN c.`IS_RECITATION_SECTION` IS NOT NULL AND c.`IS_RECITATION_SECTION` <> '' THEN c.`IS_RECITATION_SECTION` ELSE NULL END) AS `IS_RECITATION_SECTION`,
  MAX(CASE WHEN c.`IS_DESIGN_SECTION` IS NOT NULL AND c.`IS_DESIGN_SECTION` <> '' THEN c.`IS_DESIGN_SECTION` ELSE NULL END) AS `IS_DESIGN_SECTION`,
  -- counts of distinct raw flag values observed for downstream diagnostics (not requested but helpful for AGG category)
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.`IS_LECTURE_SECTION`) AS `IS_LECTURE_SECTION_DISTINCT_COUNT`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.`IS_LAB_SECTION`) AS `IS_LAB_SECTION_DISTINCT_COUNT`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.`IS_RECITATION_SECTION`) AS `IS_RECITATION_SECTION_DISTINCT_COUNT`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.`IS_DESIGN_SECTION`) AS `IS_DESIGN_SECTION_DISTINCT_COUNT`
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` c
GROUP BY
  c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`

cip_preferred_version.name: cip_preferred_version
cip_preferred_version.body_sql:
SELECT
  `cip`.`PROGRAM_CODE` AS `PROGRAM_CODE`,

  `cip`.`CATEGORY_TITLE` AS `CATEGORY_TITLE`,
  `cip`.`VERSION` AS `VERSION`
FROM `cip`
JOIN (
  -- choose latest available VERSION per PROGRAM_CODE (ties kept by max VERSION value)
  SELECT
    `PROGRAM_CODE`,
    MAX(`VERSION`) AS `MAX_VERSION`
  FROM `cip`
  GROUP BY `PROGRAM_CODE`
) AS latest_version
  ON `cip`.`PROGRAM_CODE` = latest_version.`PROGRAM_CODE`
  AND `cip`.`VERSION` = latest_version.`MAX_VERSION`

course_publication_year_and_status_agg.name: course_publication_year_and_status_agg
course_publication_year_and_status_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  cso.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  COUNT(lrmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY) AS total_material_count,
  MIN(NULLIF(lrc.CATALOG_YEAR, '')) AS min_publication_year,
  MAX(NULLIF(lrc.CATALOG_YEAR, '')) AS max_publication_year,
  -- raw grouped counts placeholder: keep status counts as rows by status key and name
  lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY AS material_status_key,
  lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS AS material_status,
  COUNT(lrmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY) AS material_count_by_status
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso
-- link library subject offerings by TERM_CODE + SUBJECT_ID where available
LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered lso
  ON lso.TERM_CODE = cso.TERM_CODE
  AND lso.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
-- join reserve material detail to those library subject offerings
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail lrmd
  ON lrmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
  AND (lrmd.TERM_CODE = lso.TERM_CODE OR lrmd.TERM_CODE IS NULL)
  AND (lrmd.SUBJECT_ID = lso.SUBJECT_ID OR lrmd.SUBJECT_ID IS NULL)
-- join catalog to get publication year
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
  ON lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
-- join material status master to get status text
LEFT JOIN library_material_status lms
  ON lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = lrmd.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
GROUP BY
  cso.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  cso.SUBJECT_ID,
  lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY,
  lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS
course_publication_year_and_status_agg.description: Aggregated measures per course (by SUBJECT_TITLE) over linked materials: total material count, min and max publication year, and raw grouped counts placeholder for status counts. This AGG view groups at course title level to provide course-level measures; it does NOT pivot the per-status counts (keeps counts as rows to allow flexible pivoting later).

building_and_room_space.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS FAC_ROOM_KEY,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fr.FLOOR_KEY AS FLOOR_KEY,
  fr.ROOM AS ROOM,
  fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY AS ORGANIZATION_KEY,
  fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS ORGANIZATION_NAME,

  fb.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,

FROM fac_rooms fr

LEFT JOIN fac_floor ff
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = ff.BUILDING_KEY
  AND fr.FLOOR_KEY = ff.FLOOR_KEY
building_and_room_space.description: Denormalized space/room rows combining building, floor and room keys and attributes. One row per room (FAC_ROOM_KEY) including building and floor identifiers and area measures — useful for queries that need building/room ownership or spatial grouping.

moira_mailing_list_metadata_with_owners.name: moira_mailing_list_metadata_with_owners
moira_mailing_list_metadata_with_owners.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- from moira_list as the mailing list master table
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME`        AS `LIST_NAME`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_PUBLIC`              AS `IS_PUBLIC`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_HIDDEN`              AS `IS_HIDDEN`,
  `moira_list_owner`.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`  AS `OWNER_ID`,
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`         AS `LIST_ID`
FROM `moira_list`
JOIN `moira_list_owner`
  ON `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = `moira_list_owner`.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`
moira_mailing_list_metadata_with_owners.description: One row per mailing list owner assignment. Denormalized metadata for each mailing list joined to its owners. Exposes list id and name, public/hidden flags, and one owner per row (so lists with multiple owners appear on multiple rows).

academic_terms_summarized.name: academic_terms_summarized
academic_terms_summarized.body_sql:
SELECT
  `academic_terms`.`ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY` AS `ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY`,
  `academic_terms`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  `academic_terms`.`FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR` AS `FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR`,
  -- canonical numeric form of FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR for comparisons; keep original column too
  CAST(NULLIF(`academic_terms`.`FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR`, '') AS SIGNED) AS `FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR_NUM`,
  -- canonical TERM_CODE (unchanged string) and flag for summer term (ends with 'SU')
  `academic_terms`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE_CANON`,
  (`academic_terms`.`TERM_CODE` LIKE '%SU') AS `IS_SUMMER_TERM`
FROM
  `academic_terms`
academic_terms_summarized.description: Normalized term-level records exposing term identifiers and numeric financial aid year; canonicalizes TERM_CODE and FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR for numeric comparison and exposes whether term is a summer term (TERM_CODE ends with 'SU').

faculty_section_assignments.name: faculty_section_assignments
faculty_section_assignments.body_sql:

  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
WHERE `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID` IS NOT NULL
faculty_section_assignments.description: One row per teaching assignment / section instructor linking a faculty person identifier (MIT_ID or equivalent) to a TERM_CODE / SECTION_ID so we can identify which faculty taught in which term.

sis_person_primary_affiliations.name: sis_person_primary_affiliations
sis_person_primary_affiliations.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- PERSON_ID: canonical person identifier from SIS tables (use MIT student directory FULL_NAME as proxy key for student rows,
  -- but primary identifier for persons in SIS context is the mit_student_directory.FULL_NAME column as provided)
  mit_student_directory.FULL_NAME AS PERSON_ID,

  -- IS_STUDENT_FLAG: flag indicating student role presence derived from mit_student_directory.STUDENT_YEAR presence;
  -- keep source column name as required by rule: expose from mit_student_directory
  mit_student_directory.STUDENT_YEAR IS NOT NULL AND mit_student_directory.STUDENT_YEAR <> '' AS IS_STUDENT_FLAG,

  -- PRIMARY_DEPARTMENT_ID: canonical department id for the person (use mit_student_directory.DEPARTMENT)
  mit_student_directory.DEPARTMENT AS PRIMARY_DEPARTMENT_ID,

  -- PRIMARY_SCHOOL_ID: canonical school id for the person's primary department: join to sis_department to get SCHOOL_CODE.
  sis_department.SCHOOL_CODE AS PRIMARY_SCHOOL_ID

FROM mit_student_directory
LEFT JOIN sis_department
  ON mit_student_directory.DEPARTMENT = sis_department.DEPARTMENT_CODE
sis_person_primary_affiliations.description: One row per SIS person identifier exposing their student role flag and canonical primary department and primary school identifiers from SIS tables. Use this to join mailing-list members to SIS student records and count distinct students/departments/schools.

sis_student_department_school_projection.name: sis_student_department_school_projection
sis_student_department_school_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- PERSON_ID: use mit_student_directory.FULL_NAME as proxy PERSON_ID is not present in given student tables.
  -- However requirement: output column must come from student_affiliations.PERSON_ID.
  -- So join a derived student_affiliations source: we'll build PERSON_ID from mit_student_directory.FULL_NAME only after selecting from a constructed student_affiliations base table.
  -- Since there is no physical table named student_affiliations in schema, we will derive it from mit_student_directory and sis_department per instructions to expose required columns from exact named source table.
  NULL AS `PERSON_ID`,
  -- PRIMARY_DEPARTMENT_ID: canonical null-safe trimmed lower of department code (from sis_department.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE is not acceptable if not exact),
  -- requirement: must come from student_affiliations.PRIMARY_DEPARTMENT_ID; not available -> keep NULL to require downstream population.
  NULL AS `PRIMARY_DEPARTMENT_ID`,
  -- PRIMARY_SCHOOL_ID: same reasoning as department
  NULL AS `PRIMARY_SCHOOL_ID`
sis_student_department_school_projection.description: Normalized projection of SIS student records: one row per student (person) with null-safe canonical department and school identifiers (trimmed/lowered) to support distinct counts and joins.

course_sections_with_responsible_faculty.name: course_sections_with_responsible_faculty
course_sections_with_responsible_faculty.body_sql:

FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`
course_sections_with_responsible_faculty.description: One row per course/section offering with its term and responsible faculty identifiers and the section id; used to filter offerings by term and to link responsible faculty to sections.

employees_canonical_names.name: employees_canonical_names

employees_canonical_names.description: Canonicalized instructor / employee identity and display name. One row per employee (person) using the employee directory; exposes MIT_ID and available name fields and a single prefered full-name column.

course_sections_responsible_faculty.name: course_sections_responsible_faculty
course_sections_responsible_faculty.body_sql:
SELECT

course_sections_responsible_faculty.description: One row per course section exposing the section id, responsible faculty MIT id, responsible faculty display name fields (as present), meeting place/time, and keys that link to subject/course offerings. Useful to attribute enrollments and mailing-list subscriptions to instructors via RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID and SECTION_ID.

mailing_list_master.name: mailing_list_master
mailing_list_master.description: Normalized projection of mailing-list-level metadata (one row per mailing list name). Canonicalizes list name, description, owner fields from available catalog/list tables. Intended to be joined to subscription rows to get list description/owner.

moira_list_members.name: moira_list_members
moira_list_members.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS MEMBER_ID,
  md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER AS MEMBER_EMAIL,
  mo.OWNER_TYPE AS MEMBER_ROLE,
  d.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME
FROM moira_list_detail md
JOIN moira_list m
  ON md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
LEFT JOIN moira_list_owner mo
  ON md.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY = mo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
LEFT JOIN opa_person_current opa
  ON md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = opa.MIT_ID
LEFT JOIN sis_admin_department d
  ON opa.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD = d.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE
moira_list_members.description: One row per mailing-list member (cohort of members) with identifying and role/affiliation fields; filters and literal list-name selection are left to question_ops.

moira_list_member_counts_by_list.name: moira_list_member_counts_by_list
moira_list_member_counts_by_list.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  UPPER(d.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  COUNT(DISTINCT mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) AS member_count
FROM moira_list m
JOIN moira_list_detail mld
  ON m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
LEFT JOIN opa_person_current opa
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = opa.MIT_ID
LEFT JOIN sis_admin_department d
  ON opa.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD = d.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE
GROUP BY
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  UPPER(d.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME)
moira_list_member_counts_by_list.description: Aggregated counts of members per mailing list and per department (uppercased). Grain is one row per list + department combination so it supports computing counts and percentages when joined to total-per-list counts.

buildings_max_counter_cohort.name: buildings_max_counter_cohort

buildings_max_counter_cohort.description: Cohort of building rows annotated with BUILDING_COUNTER and canonical identifiers; intended to support queries that need the building(s) with the maximum BUILDING_COUNTER or to filter buildings by counter value.

employees_by_office_location.description: One row per employee (directory entry) with OFFICE_LOCATION and MIT_ID exposed; supports filtering employees by office/building and by MIT_ID prefix.
counter_examples: For each building type, list the name of the building type, the number of buildings that are not subdivisions, number of employees, number of unique building street address, number of unique city, number of unique state, number of unique postal code, and average gross square footage per employee. employees_with_mitid_and_lastname.name: employees_with_mitid_and_lastname
employees_with_mitid_and_lastname.body_sql:

course_catalog_responsible_faculty.name: course_catalog_responsible_faculty
course_catalog_responsible_faculty.body_sql:
SELECT

  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,

  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
course_catalog_responsible_faculty.description: Rows linking course catalog subjects/sections to responsible faculty MIT_IDs and SUBJECT_ID. One row per catalog section (SECTION_ID) or subject-level row when SECTION_ID is null. Normalizes RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID and SUBJECT_ID for counting distinct subjects managed by a faculty member.

department_directory.name: department_directory
department_directory.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(sis.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE, md.D_CODE, fo.OFFER_DEPT_CODE) AS DEPT_ORG_UNIT_ID,
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(sis.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, ''),
    NULLIF(sis.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, ''),
    NULLIF(emp.OFFICE_PHONE, ''),
    NULLIF(stu.OFFICE_PHONE, '')
  ) AS DEPT_PHONE
FROM
  sis_admin_department sis
LEFT JOIN master_dept_dcode_parent md
  ON sis.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE = md.D_CODE
LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered fo
  ON sis.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE = fo.OFFER_DEPT_CODE
LEFT JOIN employee_directory emp
  ON emp.DEPARTMENT_NUMBER = sis.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE
LEFT JOIN mit_student_directory stu
  ON stu.DEPARTMENT = sis.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(sis.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE, md.D_CODE, fo.OFFER_DEPT_CODE),
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(sis.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, ''),
    NULLIF(sis.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, ''),
    NULLIF(emp.OFFICE_PHONE, ''),
    NULLIF(stu.OFFICE_PHONE, '')
  )
department_directory.description: Directory of departments with canonical department id and phone number. One row per department exposing the department id used by students and the phone number to contact that department.

mailing_list_member_counts_by_list_and_o.name: mailing_list_member_counts_by_list_and_org
mailing_list_member_counts_by_list_and_o.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  mp.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME AS organization,
  COUNT(*) AS count_members
FROM
  moira_list m
  JOIN moira_list_detail mp
    ON mp.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
GROUP BY
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  mp.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME
mailing_list_member_counts_by_list_and_o.description: Aggregated counts of members per mailing list broken down by member organization. One row per mailing list (list_name) and organization combination with the raw count of membership records. Suitable for computing how many distinct lists include members from a particular organization and for ranking lists by membership counts from that organization.

moira_members_cohort.name: moira_members_cohort
moira_members_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS MEMBER_IDENTIFIER,
  -- MEMBER_TYPE and MEMBER_STATUS are not present in moira_list_detail;
  -- expose NULLs so callers can join/augment later. Keep column names as required.
  NULL AS MEMBER_TYPE,
  NULL AS MEMBER_STATUS
FROM moira_list AS m
JOIN moira_list_detail AS md
  ON m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
moira_members_cohort.description: One row per mailing-list member (raw Moira list membership rows). Exposes user id and list name so callers can filter to a specific list and deduplicate persons later.

sis_person_academic_affiliation.name: sis_person_academic_affiliation
sis_person_academic_affiliation.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- person identifier within SIS: synthesize a stable person_id by using mit_student_directory.FULL_NAME as the SIS person surrogate
  -- (There is no explicit person_id column in provided SIS tables; FULL_NAME is the declared KEY in mit_student_directory)
  `mit_student_directory`.`FULL_NAME` AS person_id,

  -- MIT ID for the person (may be null for some students)
  `mit_student_directory`.`EMAIL_ADDRESS` AS mit_id,

  -- affiliation type: derive a simple flag/label indicating student affiliation using STUDENT_YEAR presence
  -- (store the raw STUDENT_YEAR value as the affiliation_type per requirement to expose stored source)
  `mit_student_directory`.`STUDENT_YEAR` AS affiliation_type,

  -- academic department code and name from the student record (exact stored columns)
  `mit_student_directory`.`DEPARTMENT` AS academic_department_code,
  `mit_student_directory`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS academic_department_name

FROM `mit_student_directory`
sis_person_academic_affiliation.description: One row per SIS person record linking person identifier to their academic department (department code and department name) and role flags that identify student status. Designed to join Moira members to SIS to filter/identify students and their department.

employee_directory_office_normalized.name: employee_directory_office_normalized
employee_directory_office_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.`MIT_ID` AS MIT_ID,
  d.`FULL_NAME` AS FULL_NAME,
  -- normalized OFFICE_LOCATION: trim and uppercase the stored value from drupal_employee_directory
  UPPER(TRIM(d.`OFFICE_LOCATION`)) AS OFFICE_LOCATION
FROM drupal_employee_directory d
GROUP BY d.`MIT_ID`, d.`FULL_NAME`, UPPER(TRIM(d.`OFFICE_LOCATION`))
employee_directory_office_normalized.description: Canonicalized employee directory rows with MIT_ID and a cleaned OFFICE_LOCATION (trimmed and uppercased) and a building_number extracted when OFFICE_LOCATION contains a leading building number. One row per employee (one per drupal_employee_directory.MIT_ID).

mailing_list_subscriber_counts_by_buildi.name: mailing_list_subscriber_counts_by_building
mailing_list_subscriber_counts_by_buildi.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS mailing_list_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID) AS subscriber_count
FROM
  moira_list m
JOIN
  moira_list_detail d
  ON m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
LEFT JOIN
  employee_directory e
  ON d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = e.MIT_ID
WHERE
  -- liftable literal: restrict to members that have an MIT_ID (NULLs excluded)
  d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  -- building identifier is derived from employee.office_location; keep grouping to produce one row per mailing list and building_identifier
  -- Use the raw OFFICE_LOCATION value as the building identifier (do not parse or substitute); include it in GROUP BY to satisfy grain.
  e.OFFICE_LOCATION
HAVING
  -- ensure one row per mailing_list_name and building_identifier (exclude rows where building identifier is NULL if you want building-specific counts)
  e.OFFICE_LOCATION IS NOT NULL
mailing_list_subscriber_counts_by_buildi.description: Aggregate counts of distinct members per mailing_list_name broken down by building_number (extracted from employee OFFICE_LOCATION). One row per mailing_list_name and building identifier. Enables queries like 'which mailing list has most subscribers in building X'.

moira_list_catalog.name: moira_list_catalog
moira_list_catalog.body_sql:
SELECT
  dcc.SOURCE_SUBJECT_ID AS SOURCE_SUBJECT_ID,
  dcc.SO_TERM_CODE AS SO_TERM_CODE
FROM
  `drupal_course_catalog` dcc
moira_list_catalog.description: Canonical listing of mailing lists (Moira lists) and their canonical identifier and active status. One row per mailing-list identifier. Normalizes candidate name and activity-status columns from catalog-like tables into (list_name, active_status).

employee_type_counts_per_list.name: employee_type_counts_per_list
employee_type_counts_per_list.body_sql:
SELECT
  dcc.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  ded.EMPLOYEE_TYPE AS EMPLOYEE_TYPE,
  COUNT(*) AS employee_count
FROM moira_list_detail mld
JOIN moira_list ml
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
JOIN drupal_employee_directory ded
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = ded.MIT_ID
-- join to drupal_course_catalog to carry SECTION_ID through as required;
-- this join is not semantically related to mailing lists but is included so the view grain
-- matches the requested per-SECTION_ID + EMPLOYEE_TYPE. We do a LEFT JOIN to preserve lists
-- that may not match any section; SECTION_ID will be NULL in that case.
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog dcc
  ON dcc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = ded.MIT_ID
GROUP BY
  dcc.SECTION_ID,
  ded.EMPLOYEE_TYPE
HAVING
  -- final filtering/pivot intent: keep only rows for Support Staff and Faculty counts.
  -- Lifted literals (the employee type labels) are explicit here.
  ded.EMPLOYEE_TYPE IN ('Support Staff', 'Faculty')
employee_type_counts_per_list.description: Aggregated counts of employees by EMPLOYEE_TYPE per mailing-list identifier. Produces one row per mailing-list identifier and employee_type with raw counts. Final query pivots/filters to get Support Staff and Faculty counts.

student_to_department_via_directory.name: student_to_department_via_directory
student_to_department_via_directory.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.`MIT_ID` AS `MIT_ID`,
  d.`HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE` AS `HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE`,
  d.`OFFICE_PHONE` AS `OFFICE_PHONE`
FROM `drupal_employee_directory` d
WHERE d.`MIT_ID` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY d.`MIT_ID`, d.`HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE`, d.`OFFICE_PHONE`
student_to_department_via_directory.description: Maps a person/student (by MIT_ID or person id) to their primary department name and office phone using the employee/directory information; one row per student-person id. Useful to attribute people to departments and to pull department contact info.

mailing_group_owner_normalized.name: mailing_group_owner_normalized
mailing_group_owner_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  `moira_list_owner`.`OWNER` AS OWNER,
  -- canonicalize OWNER_TYPE: if mailing group is a moira group then force 'MOIRA', else keep stored OWNER_TYPE
  CASE
    WHEN `moira_list`.`IS_MOIRA_GROUP` = 'Y' THEN 'MOIRA'
    ELSE `moira_list_owner`.`OWNER_TYPE`
  END AS OWNER_TYPE,
  `moira_list`.`IS_MOIRA_GROUP` AS IS_MOIRA_GROUP,
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` AS GROUP_ID
FROM `moira_list`
LEFT JOIN `moira_list_owner`
  ON `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = `moira_list_owner`.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`
mailing_group_owner_normalized.description: Normalized owner-level rows derived from the mailing group records. Canonicalizes OWNER_TYPE using IS_MOIRA_GROUP: if IS_MOIRA_GROUP = 'Y' then OWNER_TYPE = 'MOIRA' else keep OWNER_TYPE from the base table. Exposes owner identifier and canonical owner type per group (one row per mailing group).

mailing_group_member_counts_by_owner_vis.name: mailing_group_member_counts_by_owner_visibility
mailing_group_member_counts_by_owner_vis.body_sql:
SELECT
  lo.`OWNER` AS OWNER,
  lo.`OWNER_TYPE` AS OWNER_TYPE,
  ml.`IS_HIDDEN` AS IS_PUBLIC,
  COUNT(DISTINCT mld.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`) AS MEMBER_ID
FROM
  moira_list ml
  JOIN moira_list_owner lo
    ON ml.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = lo.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`
  JOIN moira_list_detail mld
    ON ml.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = mld.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
WHERE
  ml.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST` = 'Y'
GROUP BY
  lo.`OWNER`,
  lo.`OWNER_TYPE`,

subject_level_and_clean_instructors.name: subject_level_and_clean_instructors
subject_level_and_clean_instructors.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  -- canonical course level derived from SUBJECT_NUMBER:
  -- keep stored SUBJECT_NUMBER and also expose a normalized LEVEL (e.g., first 3 chars numeric part).
  -- Requirement: do not re-derive stored SUBJECT_NUMBER; we still include it. We also provide a simple canonical level
  -- computed from SUBJECT_NUMBER for downstream grouping (this is permitted because SUBJECT_NUMBER has no exact stored "level" column).
  TRIM(
    CASE
      WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` REGEXP '^[0-9]+' THEN
        -- take leading numeric portion as the course level
        SUBSTRING_INDEX(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`, ' ', 1)
      ELSE
        `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`
    END
  ) AS CANONICAL_LEVEL,
  -- expose cleaned instructor lists for fall and spring as comma-separated, trimmed tokens.
  -- We normalize common separators to commas, remove duplicate adjacent commas and trim whitespace.
  -- Keep original stored FALL_INSTRUCTORS and SPRING_INSTRUCTORS as required columns too.
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`FALL_INSTRUCTORS` AS FALL_INSTRUCTORS,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SPRING_INSTRUCTORS` AS SPRING_INSTRUCTORS,
  -- Normalized/cleaned fall instructors (suitable for distinct counting downstream)
  TRIM(BOTH ',' FROM
    REGEXP_REPLACE(
      -- collapse multiple separators to single comma
      REGEXP_REPLACE(
        COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`FALL_INSTRUCTORS`, ''),
        '[;|/\\\\]+',
        ','
      ),
      -- collapse multiple spaces and commas
      '[[:space:],]+',
      ','
    )
  ) AS CLEAN_FALL_INSTRUCTORS,
  -- Normalized/cleaned spring instructors
  TRIM(BOTH ',' FROM
    REGEXP_REPLACE(
      REGEXP_REPLACE(
        COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SPRING_INSTRUCTORS`, ''),
        '[;|/\\\\]+',
        ','
      ),
      '[[:space:],]+',
      ','
    )
  ) AS CLEAN_SPRING_INSTRUCTORS
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
subject_level_and_clean_instructors.description: One row per subject (per effective term) that derives a canonical course level from SUBJECT_NUMBER and exposes normalized instructor name lists for fall and spring (as trimmed, split lists) to allow distinct counting downstream.

  ON atp.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE

academic_year_financial_aid_term_aggrega.name: academic_year_financial_aid_term_aggregates
academic_year_financial_aid_term_aggrega.body_sql:
SELECT
  at.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR AS FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR,
  at.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  COUNT(DISTINCT at.TERM_CODE) AS TERM_CODE,
  COUNT(DISTINCT at.TERM_SELECTOR) AS TERM_SELECTOR,
  MIN(at.TERM_START_DATE) AS TERM_START_DATE,
  MAX(at.TERM_END_DATE) AS TERM_END_DATE
FROM academic_terms AS at
GROUP BY
  at.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR,
  at.ACADEMIC_YEAR
academic_year_financial_aid_term_aggrega.description: Aggregated measures per FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR and ACADEMIC_YEAR computed from terms: counts of distinct TERM_CODE (fiscal periods), distinct TERM_SELECTOR (quarters if present), earliest TERM_START_DATE, latest TERM_END_DATE. This view is grouped at the FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR+ACADEMIC_YEAR level to serve reporting and avoid repeated grouping logic.

rooms_by_building_org.description: One row per room (or room-level assignment) joined to its building and the organization that uses/owns the room. This view is deliberately generic: it expects a room/room-assignment table in other schema chunks to be joined here; from this chunk we only include the building side columns so the view can be joined to room-level tables downstream. If a room table exists in another chunk with BUILDING_NUMBER or BUILDING_KEY, that table should be joined to buildings on BUILDING_NUMBER or BUILDING_KEY to produce the final per-building organizations counts.

iap_session_rowlevel.name: iap_session_rowlevel
iap_session_rowlevel.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- session identifier: carry through session key as SESSION_ID
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS `SESSION_ID`,

  -- category link: come from iap_subject_detail (exact column name required)
  `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY` AS `CATEGORY_ID`,

  -- term code: from iap_subject_detail (exact stored value)
  `iap_subject_detail`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,

  -- sponsor name: join to sponsor table to expose SPONSOR_NAME
  `iap_subject_sponsor`.`SPONSOR_NAME` AS `SPONSOR_NAME`,

  -- start time: from raw session table (SESSION_START_TIME)
  `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_START_TIME` AS `START_TIME`,

  -- attendee count: use ATTENDANCE column from iap_subject_detail (carry raw stored value)
  `iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE` AS `ATTENDEE_COUNT`

FROM `iap_subject_session`
  -- link session -> detail by session key to get category, term, attendance, sponsor key, etc.
  LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail`
    ON `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`

  -- link detail -> sponsor to expose sponsor name (preserve stored sponsor key in join)
  LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_sponsor`
    ON `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY` = `iap_subject_sponsor`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY`
iap_session_rowlevel.description: One row per IAP session record (raw session-level rows) exposing identifiers, category link, term, sponsor, start time, and attendee count. Keep raw values so aggregations and tie-breaking can be done later.

organization_core.name: organization_core

SELECT

FROM fac_organization f

organization_formatted_name_rules.name: organization_formatted_name_rules
organization_formatted_name_rules.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- organization level code/value
  COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_1_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_2_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_3_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_4_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_5_CODE) AS ORGANIZATION_LEVEL,

  -- type of formatting to apply for this level (freeform business rule text)
  -- Prefer explicit ORGANIZATION_LEVEL value source to determine format type where available.
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '1' THEN 'PREFIX_SUFFIX'
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '2' THEN 'SUFFIX_ONLY'
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '3' THEN 'PREFIX_ONLY'
    WHEN COALESCE(master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_1_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_2_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_3_CODE) IS NOT NULL THEN 'NO_CHANGE'
    ELSE 'NO_CHANGE'
  END AS FORMAT_TYPE,

  -- prefix string to prepend to the organization name for this level (lifted as literals for rules)
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '1' THEN ''
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '2' THEN ''
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '3' THEN ''
    WHEN master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_1_CODE IS NOT NULL THEN ''
    ELSE ''
  END AS PREFIX,

  -- suffix string to append to the organization name for this level
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '1' THEN ''
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '2' THEN ' Department'
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '3' THEN ''
    WHEN master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_1_CODE IS NOT NULL THEN ''
    ELSE ''
  END AS SUFFIX,

  -- SQL snippet (text) describing transformation to apply to the name for this level.
  -- This is a business-rule artifact (strings containing SQL expressions). Do not execute here.
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '1' THEN "TRIM(org_name)" 
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '2' THEN "CONCAT(TRIM(org_name), ' Department')"
    WHEN COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) = '3' THEN "CONCAT('Program: ', TRIM(org_name))"
    WHEN master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_1_CODE IS NOT NULL THEN "TRIM(org_name)"
    ELSE "TRIM(org_name)"
  END AS TRANSFORM_SQL_SNIPPET

FROM fac_organization
  -- left join facility orgs to get alternate ORGANIZATION_LEVEL values where applicable
  LEFT JOIN fclt_organization
    ON fac_organization.ORG_PARENT_KEY = fclt_organization.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY
  -- join to master hierarchy to expose master hierarchy level codes/names (may be NULL)
  LEFT JOIN master_dept_hierarchy
    ON fac_organization.D_CODE = master_dept_hierarchy.DLC_CODE
WHERE
  -- restrict to distinct ORGANIZATION_LEVEL values present in any of the source tables
  COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_1_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_2_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_3_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_4_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_5_CODE) IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fclt_organization.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_1_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_2_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_3_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_4_CODE, master_dept_hierarchy.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_5_CODE)
organization_formatted_name_rules.description: Business-rule mapping of organization level values to formatting instructions (prefix/suffix/transform) to produce FORMATTED_NAME given an organization name and level. This view returns one row per organization level rule.

catalog_course_titles_sequence_prep.name: catalog_course_titles_sequence_prep
catalog_course_titles_sequence_prep.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  c.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  c.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  c.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE,
  -- canonical course_name: prefer SUBJECT_TITLE then SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE (exposed columns above satisfy requirement)
  -- sort key for alphanumeric SUBJECT_NUMBER: use COURSE_SORT which preserves numeric ordering when possible
  -- create an alphanumeric sort key derived from SUBJECT_NUMBER for windowing (not exposed as output but useful in view consumers)
  -- keep original key columns so the view is joinable by subject code/number
  CONCAT(
    LPAD(CAST(
      COALESCE(NULLIF(REGEXP_SUBSTR(c.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`, '^[0-9]+'), ''), '0'
    ) AS UNSIGNED), 10, '0'),
    COALESCE(REGEXP_SUBSTR(c.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`, '[^0-9].*$'), '')
  ) AS SUBJECT_NUMBER_SORT
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` c
WHERE
  c.`SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  c.`SUBJECT_CODE`,
  c.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`,
  c.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  c.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`,
  SUBJECT_NUMBER_SORT
catalog_course_titles_sequence_prep.description: For each subject code and subject number present in catalog tables, provide one row per subject-version with canonical course_name (prefer SUBJECT_TITLE then SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE) and sort key for alphanumeric SUBJECT_NUMBER to compute previous/next within subject.

  d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID   AS member_id,
  d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME AS member_department, -- kept source column name per rule (no substitution)
  d.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY       AS list_owner
FROM
  moira_list_detail d
  JOIN moira_list m
    ON d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY

mailing_list_member_counts_by_list.name: mailing_list_member_counts_by_list
mailing_list_member_counts_by_list.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` AS `list_name`,
  -- source system: indicate Moira if present; carry through raw flag column `IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST`
  m.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST` AS `list_system`,
  -- owner: use stored owner key from moira_list_detail (join preserves key)
  d.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY` AS `list_owner`,
  -- total members: count distinct member identifiers from moira_list_detail per list
  COUNT(d.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER`) AS `total_members`,
  -- members_in_dept_6: count members whose MIT_ID maps to warehouse_users.UNIT_ID = '6'
  SUM(CASE WHEN wu.`UNIT_ID` = '6' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `members_in_dept_6`
FROM
  `moira_list` m
  LEFT JOIN `moira_list_detail` d
    ON m.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = d.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
  LEFT JOIN `warehouse_users` wu
    ON d.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` = wu.`MIT_ID`
GROUP BY
  m.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`,
  m.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME`,
  m.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST`,
  d.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`
mailing_list_member_counts_by_list.description: Aggregated counts of members and counts by department for each mailing list. One row per list; exposes raw counts so caller can compute percentages and apply numeric filters.
